newsitem.title: USA: Fla. tobacco suit vs. R.J. Reynolds delayed.
newsitem.headline: Fla. tobacco suit vs. R.J. Reynolds delayed.

text.p: The trial of a wrongful death lawsuit filed against RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co by the sister of a smoker who died of lung cancer has been indefinitely postponed, an attorney for the plaintiff said Tuesday.
The lawsuit, which was set to go to trial on Nov. 4 in Jacksonville, may be tried in 1997, said attorney Stephanie Hartley.
The suit claims the death of Jean Connor was the result of negligence on the part of R.J. Reynolds, as well as Winn-Dixie Stores Inc and Lil' Champ as sellers of cigarettes.
The suit, initially filed in 1995 on behalf of Connor, was refiled following her death with her sister, Dana Raulerson, as the plaintiff.
Hartley said the trial was delayed at the request of the plaintiff to allow new allegations of conspiracy and claims of punitive damages to be included.

"We felt that because she (Connor) smoked as a minor, the punitive damages case was very good against R.J. Reynolds," she said, adding that the case could be tried in February, April or June next year.
